292:   #result(id, accepted, error) {
293:     if (!this.linkActive || !this.nonce || typeof id !== "string" ||
294:         Buffer.byteLength(id, "utf8") > MAX_REQUEST_ID_BYTES) return;
295:     try {
296:       this.publish(assertFits({
297:         v: VERSION, type: "permission_result", connection_nonce: this.nonce,
298:         epoch: this.epoch, id, accepted, ...(error ? { error } : {}),
299:       }));
300:     } catch {
301:       /* An invalid device ID must not make bridge output exceed the link cap. */
302:     }
303:   }
304: 
305:   #onAdapterEvent(event) {
306:     try {
307:       if (event.type === "text") {
308:         event = { ...event, text: sanitizeAgentText(event.text) };
309:       }
310:       if (event.type === "session_started") {
311:         this.usage.reset(event.backend ?? this.adapter.backend);
312:         this.usageReady = true;
313:         this.usageSnapshot();
314:         return;
315:       }
316:       if (event.type === "usage") {
317:         this.usage.record(event);
318:         this.usageSnapshot();
319:         return;
320:       }
321:       if (event.type === "permission_request") {
322:         clearTimeout(this.permissionTimer);
323:         if (this.activeTurn?.device && this.activeTurn.detached) {
324:           /* The ACP turn belongs to a disconnected device. Do not rebind its
325:            * permission request to a later nonce; reject through ACP instead. */
326:           const orphaned = this.permissions.ptSubmit(event.params);
327:           const rejected = this.permissions.rejectPending();
328:           if (rejected) {
329:             this.adapter.respondPermission(rejected.id, rejected.result).catch(() => {});
330:           }
331:           return orphaned;
332:         }
333:         const snapshot = this.permissions.ptSubmit(event.params);
334:         this.facts = { ...this.facts, ...snapshot, msg: snapshot.msg };
335:         this.snapshot();
336:         this.permissionTimer = setTimeout(() => this.disconnect(), this.permissionTimeoutMs);
337:         return;
338:       }
339:       if (event.type === "tool") {
340:         if (this.activeTurn?.device && this.activeTurn.detached) {
341:           /* This tool belongs to a turn started by the disconnected nonce. */
342:           return;
343:         }
344:         clearTimeout(this.textTimer);
345:         this.textBuffer = "";
346:         this.facts.running = this.activeTurn ? 1 :
347:           (event.status === "completed" || event.status === "failed" ? 0 : 1);
348:         this.facts.msg = summarizeMessage(event.title || "Tool activity");
349:         this.snapshot();
350:         if ((event.status === "completed" || event.status === "failed") && this.nonce) {
351:           this.publish({ v: VERSION, type: "tool_result", connection_nonce: this.nonce, epoch: this.epoch, toolCallId: event.toolCallId, status: event.status });
352:         }
353:         return;
354:       }
355:       if (event.type === "text") {
356:         this.#queueOutput(event.text);
357:         this.textBuffer += event.text;
358:         if (this.textTimer) return;
359:         this.textTimer = setTimeout(() => {
360:           this.facts.msg = summarizeMessage(this.textBuffer);
361:           this.textBuffer = "";
362:           this.textTimer = null;
363:           this.snapshot();
364:         }, 120);
365:         this.textTimer.unref?.();
366:       }
367:     } finally {
368:       try { this.onAdapterEvent(event, this.currentUsage()); } catch {}
369:     }
370:   }
371: }

This is **`vela-deskmate-acp-bridge-spike`** — a Node.js library (ESM, v0.1.0) that acts as a local protocol bridge between a **DeskMate AI agent** (running via MiMoCode/ACP) and an **IoT device** (e.g. a BK7258 embedded board) communicating over MQTT.

Here's the breakdown:

**What it does**

It implements a stateful protocol bridge so a remote device can:
- Send prompts to an AI agent and receive streaming text output
- See real-time agent status snapshots (running/waiting/idle)
- Approve or deny tool-use permission requests that the agent raises
- Track token/session usage telemetry

**Key components**

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `src/protocol.js` | Wire format — message schemas, size limits (4 KiB/message, 2 KiB prompts), encode/decode helpers |
| `src/bridge-core.js` | Core state machine — manages the connection lifecycle, turn tracking, permission timeouts, output buffering and chunking |
| `src/bridge.js` | ACP-layer bridge — translates between the device protocol and the ACP (AI Coding Platform) permission model |
| `src/mqtt-transport.js` | MQTT transport — publishes/subscribes messages over an MQTT broker |
| `src/mimo-attach.js` | Attaches to a live MiMoCode agent session to drive it |
| `src/acp-adapter.js` | Adapts MiMoCode's ACP interface to the bridge's adapter contract |
| `src/session-usage.js` | Ledger tracking token/cost usage per session |
| `bin/deskmate-bridge.mjs` | Entry point — starts the bridge with a fake adapter for testing |
| `bin/deskmate-client.mjs` | Test client — simulates a device connecting over MQTT |

**Protocol design**

The wire protocol is newline-delimited JSON over MQTT, versioned (`v: 1`), with:
- A `connection_nonce` + `epoch` pair to detect stale connections
- At-most-once delivery semantics with idempotent request IDs for prompt re-sends
- Agent output chunked to stay under 4 KiB per message (source text capped at 1600 bytes to leave room for JSON overhead)
- A 30-second permission timeout that auto-disconnects if the device doesn't respond

**Context in the contest repo**

This lives under `tools/acp-bridge/` in the openvela 2026 contest repo (team 272, "tokenwujixian"), making it a development tool/spike rather than the contest submission itself — likely used to connect the BK7258 board to an AI agent over the local network.

This is the **contest entry repo** for team 272 ("tokenwujixian") in the **2026 openvela AI Hardware Developer Contest**.

**What's in it**

The repo serves two purposes at once:
- A **code submission** — contest work lives here and gets soft-linked into the openvela build tree via a `repo` manifest
- An **AI coding log archive** — all AI-assisted development sessions are exported to `logs/` and submitted alongside the code

**The actual work done so far**

- `chips/bk7258/` — BK7258 chip-level bringup work, including a WiFi porting plan (`OPENVELA_NUTTX_WIFI_PORTING_PLAN.md`) and a CPU0 bringup contract (README mentioned it reached NuttShell on real hardware as of 2026-08-11)
- `board/bk7258-devkit/` — board-level BSP/config for the BK7258 devkit
- `logs/C-Luv9615/` — AI coding session logs from 2026-08-18 through 2026-09-01
